decision: routed the task to figure-it-out with a committed decision trail
why: user went to sleep and will review the result later, and poteto-mode sends unattended multi-part work there

decision: definition of done: pytest green incl. mandated 1300/1500 integration test, tsc+eslint+vite build green, scripted browser run of acceptance criteria 1-16 against the real server
why: a falsifiable predicate the user can rerun instead of trusting a summary

decision: skipped the architect/arena fan-out for the overall design
why: the brief already fixes the stack, entities and most rules, so a design bakeoff would repeat settled choices; the open forks are logged here instead

decision: money is integer cents end to end (DB, API, UI formatting only at the edge); percentages as basis points
why: no floats anywhere and no Decimal-vs-string ambiguity in JSON

decision: 20/50/30 split uses a budget-model registry plus largest-remainder rounding
why: the three shares must sum exactly to the net salary and other models must be addable without new branches

decision: reserve and savings are append-only ledgers; balances are sums, never stored counters
why: every movement stays traceable and corrections are new rows instead of edits

decision: period budget per bucket = sum of allocation rows (salary split, extra income, reserve coverage)
why: extra income and deliberate reserve coverage then flow through one mechanism and close-out math stays a single formula

decision: edits that touch a closed period return 409 with the reserve delta until the client resends with confirm_correction; the delta is booked as a correction ledger row plus an audit record
why: brief 4.2 forbids silent changes to closed periods

decision: single transactions table with a type discriminator (expense, income, transfer); Income from the brief is the income subtype
why: one searchable, filterable list for the UI without unions over several tables

decision: generic idempotency-key table written in the same DB transaction as the operation, plus BEGIN IMMEDIATE on SQLite
why: double submits must not create a second period or a second reserve credit even when two requests race

decision: sessions are server-side rows (sha256 of token), cookie SameSite=Strict httpOnly, CSRF via double-submit cookie checked against the session row
why: cookie auth needs CSRF protection per brief 15; storing only the hash means a DB leak does not leak live sessions

decision: salary preview runs the real close-and-open inside a SAVEPOINT and rolls it back
why: the confirmation screen can then never disagree with what recording the salary actually does

decision: savings share is booked into the savings ledger when the salary arrives, not at period close
why: pay-yourself-first: the 20% is set aside immediately, and the brief's dashboard wants current planned savings visible

decision: incomes and transfers are cancelled with mirrored ledger rows (Storno) instead of deleted; expenses are edited/deleted
why: ledgers stay append-only and money cannot vanish or appear through a delete

decision: first run of the mandated 1300/1500 scenario failed on salary_in_future and then on session expiry; both were test-clock issues, fixed in the test harness
why: the guards behaved correctly; the test had to move the frozen clock and use a long session lifetime

decision: mandated scenario passes through the HTTP API: reserve 140 EUR, savings 260+300, new split 300/750/450
why: this is the brief's binding acceptance test

decision: full backend suite: 94 tests green, ruff clean, mypy clean
why: covers every test topic listed in brief section 19

decision: mutation check: made close-out also count the savings bucket; 16 tests went red, then restored
why: the suite passed on first run, so I checked it actually observes the money math instead of trusting green

decision: added admin CLI (backup, restore with integrity check and safety copy, reset-password, migrate, seed-demo)
why: a local single-user app needs a way back in after a forgotten password and a documented restore path

decision: bucket colors: savings #1baf7a/#199e70, fixed #2a78d6/#3987e5, leisure #eb6834/#d95926 (light/dark); always shown with text labels
why: brief mandates green/blue/orange; dataviz validator passes all-pairs in both modes, light green is below 3:1 so labels are required
